entries.title: Proverbs 16:1
segments: The preparations of the heart--the answer of the tongue; both the inward disposing of our thoughts and the outward expression of them. So according to our version.  But the literal rendering of the verse is, "To man [belong] the orderings of the heart: but from Jehovah is the answer of the tongue."  "The orderings of the heart" are the plans which it forms: "the answer of the tongue" is the granting of the heart's desire in respect to these plans when expressed in words: that is, according to some, in words of prayer to God; according to others, in arguments of persuasion addressed to men.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:2
segments: Self-flattery is the universal sin of fallen man.  The best preservative against its power is, to remember that God sees us as we are, and that he will decide our eternal destiny not according to our opinion of ourselves, but according to his own infallible judgment.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:3
segments: God gives permanent success to all who, in the diligent use of the appointed means, humbly commit their labors to him.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:4
segments: Yea, even the wicked for the day of evil; "God cannot be tempted of evil, neither tempteth he any man."

But he appoints the wicked, who are "drawn away of their own lusts and enticed" to sin, to "the day of evil," for his own glory and the welfare of his everlasting kingdom.  Most interpreters prefer to render the first clause of this verse thus: The Lord has made every thing for its corresponding end; which gives substantially the same sense.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:6
segments:
Mercy and truth; exercised by penitent sinners. 
 
  Purged; expiated.  The meritorious ground of forgiveness is not here considered, but the character to which God gives pardon and salvation.  Compare

. 
 
Though no good works can merit forgiveness of sin, God will bestow it only upon those who diligently practise them, for they are the certain fruits of repentance and faith.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:7
segments: To be at peace with him; that is, as far as his best good and that of the church of God require.

God sometimes allows his servants to be persecuted for righteousness' sake. 
 
The good man's enemies are entirely in God's power.  He has only to do his duty, and God will either turn their hatred into love, or overrule it for his good and that of his church.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:9
segments: Our plans accomplish not what we intend, but what God sees to be best for us and his cause.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:10
segments:
A divine sentence; God has appointed him to administer justice in his behalf. 
 
  Transgresseth not; or, should not transgress.  Here and in
the king is described according to the true nature of his office.  When he acts in character, his mouth transgresseth not in judgment.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:11
segments:
The Lord's--his work; he has ordained them as the means of justice, and requires that they be true. 
 
  The bag; in which travelling merchants anciently carried their weights. 
 
Uprightness in our dealings with each other is a matter not of human convenience, but of divine requirement, and God will punish the want of it by exclusion from heaven.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:12
segments: There is but one law for rulers and private persons--righteousness and prosperity, or wickedness and ruin.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:13
segments: Upright rulers will surround themselves with men of truth.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:15
segments: As a cloud of the latter rain; acceptable and refreshing.  The descriptions in this and the preceding verse are peculiarly applicable to the governments of the East, where the power of the monarch is well-nigh unlimited.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:17
segments: Highway of the upright; in which they walk securely.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:19
segments: The conqueror who enriches himself by the spoils of nations is great in the eyes of sinners, but the meek and lowly Christian is great in the eyes of God.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:21
segments:
Lips; the teacher's lips. 
 
  Learning; the learning of those whom he instructs. 
 
A pleasant and winning manner, not less than soundness of doctrine, is the duty of every teacher, for his success depends mainly upon it.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:22
segments: The instruction of fools is folly; if they undertake to teach, they can communicate nothing but folly.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:26
segments: Craveth it of him; men's bodily wants urge them on to hard toil.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:27
segments: Diggeth up evil; industriously toils at his mischievous plans.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:28
segments: No person is more abhorred and avoided than the slanderer and whisperer, whose course is marked by the creation of strife and dissension among brethren.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:30
segments: Shutteth his eyes--moving his lips; signs of secret mischief.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:32
segments: The mighty conqueror who has not learned to urle his own spirit leads a miserable life, and will come to a miserable end.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:33
segments: Cast into the lap--the whole disposing thereof; man casts the lot, but God decides the issue of it.
